title: Chroma-preserve palettes, variable type scale, density-aware spacing, and layered soft elevation
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Modernize the token set for the 2026 component refresh by introducing chroma-preserving color stops, a variable (fluid) type scale, density-aware spacing/radius rules, and a layered soft elevation system optimized for data-dense tables and charts. This ticket coordinates design decisions, spec artifacts, dev constraints, and rollout notes so Engineering and Product teams can implement without regressions.

Scope:
- Create a palette recipe that preserves perceived chroma when lightness changes (works for light/dark themes and interactive states).
- Define 5 perceptual color stop tiers (neutral, low-accent, accent, critical, success) with accessible contrast targets at each stop.
- Author a variable type scale (responsive clamp-based tokens) with token aliases for ui/surface/content/caption that work across breakpoints.
- Define density-aware spacing and radius tokens: default, compact, and dense variants; include explicit rules for table rows, cell padding, and chart gutters.
- Replace the current single-drop shadow with layered soft elevation tokens (surface, card, modal) that scale by density and theme.
- Provide migration guidance and a compatibility map from old tokens to new tokens for components: button, input, table, datagrid, chart axes, and toasts.

Out of scope:
- Full chart color palette overhaul for brand campaigns (handled in separate PRD).
- Per-component visual QA in each browser/device (will be follow-up testing tasks).

Acceptance criteria:
- Token spec published in the design drive doc with examples and contrast checks for each stop.
- Figma library updated with named token styles and density variants.
- Engineering design token JSON schema (tokens-2026.03) and a migration map submitted as a GitHub PR targeting the tokens repo.
- Two components (Table and Button) are implemented with new tokens in a staging branch and validated by visual diffs and performance checks.
- Runbook created for rollout with feature flag gating and fallbacks to previous tokens for hotfixes.

2026-03-01 — PM check-in (Luis Ortega): Confirmed release window tokens-2026.03 and requested that migration map include telemetry gating points. Added label 'charts' because chart gutters are impacted.

2026-03-05 — Engineering PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tokens/pull/412 — contains JSON schema and preview CSS custom properties. Requesting design signoff on semantic names and fallback values.
2026-03-08 — Sofia R: Updated acceptance criteria to add visual-diff baseline for Table and Button. Uploaded Figma file version 14 with density variants (Figma: https://figma.com/file/xyz).

2026-03-10 — Design decision: Adopt perceptual lab-based contrast checks and generate separate token sets for light/dark to avoid runtime recomputation. Decision doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DES/Chroma-Preserve-Decision
notes: Implementation notes: engineering prefers exported CSS custom properties + a light/dark precomputed token JSON to minimize runtime CPU. For small screens the variable scale clamps to a single-step reduction. Migration strategy: feature-flag rollout per tenant, with toggle to legacy tokens and an automated visual diff job to detect regressions.
qa_plan: 1) Unit tests for token exports (value validation) 2) Visual diff job for Button and Table across default/compact/dense 3) Accessibility checks: color contrast automated report for each token vs background 4) Performance test to ensure token lookup does not add >1ms per render on list-heavy pages
implementation_notes: Map old tokens to new aliases in migration map file. Add a small shim in the tokens runtime that reads feature flag 'tokens_v2' and loads tokens-2026.03 JSON. Provide compatibility layer names in tokens-legacy.json until full rollout.
